title: Regional performance anchors and cost-normalized profile publishing
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Verified performance profiles currently assume a single, global baseline. Regional differences in hardware, cloud networking, and instance types produce material variance in latency, throughput, and per-token cost. Without region-aware normalization, published Redwood-verified profiles are either overly conservative (hurting customers in high-performing regions) or underrepresentative (causing SLA misses and surprise cost regressions).

Goal: Produce a repeatable, auditable publishing flow that attaches per-region "performance anchors" and a cost-normalization factor to every Redwood-verified profile. The manifest should: (1) record measured latency and throughput distributions per-region, (2) publish a normalized cost delta relative to the canonical baseline, and (3) include gating rules for publishing and automated rollbacks when region variance exceeds thresholds.

Deliverables:
- A standardized "performance anchor manifest" artifact produced by the verification pipeline (JSON schema + signed metadata).
- Normalization algorithm and thresholds (p50/p95 delta, KV cache hit adjustment, and quantization uplift factors).
- CI pipeline step that computes per-region anchors as part of model onboarding and attaches them to the profile during publish.
- Console surface (per-profile page) showing region anchors and expected cost delta estimation.
- Canary rollout plan: publish with anchors in two regions (us-west-2, eu-central-1) before global release.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change runtime routing policies or implement cross-region routing — only the profiling and publishing artifacts and visibility that feed downstream routing decisions.
updates: 2025-03-10 - Scoped initial spec and circulated to Runtime and Observability teams. Requested data export from production verified-runner jobs (ENG-32211).
2025-03-12 - Design review with DES-421: decided on single artifact per model-version with an array of region anchors rather than separate region profiles to keep publish flow atomic.

2025-03-14 - Trade-off discussion: choose normalization to be multiplicative on per-token cost (rather than additive) to keep percentile math stable across seq lengths. Documented rationale in Confluence.

2025-03-16 - Infra/Eng scoped required telemetry: latency histograms (p50,p95,p99), throughput (tokens/sec), KV cache hit-rate, instance type, and sample-seed. ENG-32900 opened to add missing tags to verified-runner.

2025-03-18 - Prototype pipeline created: github.com/redwood-inference/verified-profiles/pull/8345 computes anchors from nightly runs. Initial results show eu-central-1 median latency 12% higher and cost delta +8% for the same model-quantization.

2025-03-20 - UX: Console mockups added to Figma and linked. DES feedback: surface a simple "expected cost delta" callout and an expandable detailed anchor table. Link: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/profile-anchors
2025-03-22 - Security sign-off scoped: no secrets in artifacts; manifests will be signed by publish CI; security review requested but low risk. (security_review_required: false).
2025-03-25 - Canary plan approved: publish anchored profile behind a feature flag in us-west-2 and eu-central-1 with 72h telemetry collection before global rollout. Added ENG canary task ENG-33177.
acceptance_criteria: Performance anchor manifest schema merged to specs repo and documented in Confluence.
CI step computes and attaches region anchors for every verified run and stores artifact in the profile registry.
Console shows the region anchors and computed cost-delta on the profile page with links to the raw telemetry dashboard.
Canary publish completed in two regions with no customer-visible regressions and telemetry collected for 72h.
Rollback/auto-block rule: if any region's p95 latency increases by >20% vs baseline OR cost-delta > 25%, the publish is blocked and a revert is triggered.
Docs and onboarding checklist updated: model owner checklist, required telemetry tags, and release runbook.
notes: We chose a multiplicative normalization factor applied to canonical per-token cost; additive approaches break across variable sequence lengths and batching regimes.
Trade-off: Single artifact reduces publish fragmentation but requires careful gating to avoid blocking model publishes for noisy regions. Canary gating reduces risk.
Next steps: finalize schema, add a signed manifest to the profile registry, and schedule a 2-week canary window.
